edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: average-risk adults in organised screening programs
edges.mechanism: FIT works by flagging occult blood from early lesions, shifting diagnosis toward more curable colorectal cancers when participation is high.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2019 Jodal meta analysis in BMJ Open already points to fit screening tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
